svg.text: REPORT 2 · FRAME 1 OF 4
PROJECT SUMMARY ANALYTICS
The whole CoForge build, measured: 11 active days, 81 commits, 444 of your turns, and what it would have cost.
Read this frame first. It is the shape of the project; the other three explain how it holds together.

g.text: Four phases: build the system, give it a design language, move that language into Figma, then point it at real work
Every figure below is counted from the git history and the session logs. Nothing is estimated.
Each column is scaled against itself. Comparing across columns is meaningless — that is why they are five charts, not one.
The system that builds: 14 agents, the routing
table, Gate A/B, the artifact taxonomy, ADR-001
Brand approved at Gate A, 829 tokens across
five axes, and the first L1 primitives.
Token release 0.2.0 is cut, tokens reach Figma
as variables, the Carbon adapter lands 208
components, CI runs the audit on a real PR.
The system is pointed at real work: Batch 3,
Each phase's hours are rounded on their own, so the four add up to 23.7h against an exact total of 23.6h. The total is the measured figure; the parts are the rounded ones.
66 percent of the cost is the agents re-reading their own conversation
Illustrative only — nothing was billed at these rates. Opus 5 list price, one-hour cache. Total $2,278.
A long agent session re-sends the whole conversation every single turn, so the same words are paid for again and again.
That re-reading is 66% of the bill. The work the agents actually produced is 8%.
The work is lumpy, not steady — and the two measures agree
Same days, same order, two separate scales. Reading one against the other is the point.
Words written by the agents, per day
Sep 7 is the single biggest day on both measures: the findings dashboard was built, attacked by two agents, and rebuilt.
“How long did this take?” has two honest answers, 4 times apart
This is why the number is defined on the board rather than just printed. An undefined metric cannot be compared to anything.
counts a minute once, however busy it was
First to last activity each day
includes every gap inside a working day
Both are honest; they answer different questions. The board uses the first, because it is the one that cannot flatter.

svg.text: What this means
The heaviest phase was not building the system — it was using
it. First application took 11.2 of the 23.6 active hours.
Cost is dominated by re-reading, not by writing. 66% of the
bill is the agents re-sending the conversation.
The work is bursty. The busiest single day, Sep 7, produced
19% of everything the agents wrote in fourteen days.
'How long did it take' has two honest answers four times
apart, so the board defines which one it uses.
What to do next
Shorten sessions, or compact them. The re-reading cost grows
with the square of the conversation length.
Keep the two time definitions in the metrics schema so future
reports stay comparable.
Point the same instrument at the next deliverable before it
starts, not after.
Get real billing figures to replace the illustrative dollars;
the token counts are already exact.

CoForge · measured from the git history and the session logs, frozen at 2026-09-08 12:11 UTC (the last record in the corpus, not the time the script ran) · every transcript record counted once, keyed on message uuid · dollars are illustrative at Opus 5 list price and were never billed
The repository counts do not include this report: it was committed after the figures were frozen, so the artifact and commit totals here are one behind by construction.
